submission.natural_language_explanation: Token-level detector, mostly in code/web/SQL text, for a small set of tokens that complete a familiar compound or code construct: 'FR' in uppercase 'I|FR|AME' (strongest, ~0.5-0.55 of max even in short text), ' FROM' after 'SELECT ...' in a SQL string, 'Select' in '.SelectCommand', 'View' ending a class name like 'ListView', '[' opening an index right after an identifier ('names[i]', 'map[string]'), and a few word-final subword pieces such as 'hel|ms', 'Blackhe|ath', 'size_|t' and ' case' in legal 'this case'/'relies on case'. Floor: the first token of every prompt gives about 0.31-0.34 of max (above the 0.25 cutoff), so every prompt counts as active; a prompt counts as strongly active only if one of these tokens rises clearly above that floor (>=0.45), and swapping the token for a near-synonym, lowercase or different spelling ('iframe', 'IGRAME', 'Insert', 'from', 'matter', 'Bristol', '(' or '.') drops the peak back to the floor.
